title: Suspected maternal sepsis
summary: Suspected sepsis in pregnancy, labour, or the puerperium — a leading cause of direct maternal death.

blocks.heading: Actions — Sepsis Six
bullets: Call for help immediately and escalate to the obstetric/medical team — maternal sepsis can progress extremely rapidly and is a leading cause of direct maternal death.

Recognise red-flag features: temperature <36°C or >38°C, tachycardia, tachypnoea, hypotension, reduced consciousness/confusion, mottled or ashen skin, non-blanching rash, or maternal concern that 'something is wrong' — VERIFY exact NEWS2/MEOWS trigger thresholds locally.

Give Sepsis Six within one hour: (1) high-flow oxygen, (2) blood cultures before antibiotics, (3) IV broad-spectrum antibiotics per local protocol, (4) IV fluid resuscitation, (5) check lactate, (6) monitor urine output — VERIFY exact antibiotic choice/dose against local protocol.
Identify likely source — consider chorioamnionitis, endometritis, urinary tract, wound/perineal infection, mastitis, pneumonia — and treat/escalate source control as needed.
Continuous maternal observations (NEWS2/MEOWS) and fetal monitoring if antenatal/intrapartum.
Involve senior obstetric, anaesthetic/critical care, and microbiology early if any red-flag feature or failure to improve.

blocks.heading: If reported by phone
bullets: If red-flag features are reported by phone (fever with rigors, feeling very unwell, confusion, breathlessness): advise her to call 999 or come to the emergency department immediately — do not wait for a routine appointment.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: Time of recognition and time help called.
NEWS2/MEOWS score and vital signs over time.
Sepsis Six elements — each with time completed.
